narr: A powerful winter storm impacted all of Southwestern California. The storm generated strong southerly winds, gusting up to 87 MPH. The storm also produced very heavy rainfall with totals up to 8 inches reported in the mountains along with numerous reports of flooding. Also, thunderstorms associated with the winter storm produced a weak tornado.
ev: Heavy rain produced flash flood and mudflows across the westbound lanes of Highway 210 in the Santa Clarita Valley. Mud flowing across the highway resulted in numerous vehicles sliding across the highway.

Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain which generated flash flooding and debris flows across the intersection of Soledad Canyon Road and Aqua Dulce Canyon Road. Significant mud, rocks and debris were reported across the intersection.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding and debris flows at the intersection of the Pacific Coast Highway and Kanan Dume Road. Numerous rocks and mud covered the intersection.
Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding near the intersection of Highway 118 and Balboa Boulevard. Three lanes of the Highway 118 were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Highway 605 and Lower Azusa Road. The onramp was flooded with over two feet of water.
Heavy rain produced significant flash flooding and debris flows at the intersection of Lake Avenue and East Altadena Drive. Mud and debris flows resulted in the closure of all three northbound lanes.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Highway 10 and Caesar Chavez Boulevard. Multiple vehicles were disabled due to the flooding.
